portfolio.shortDescription: A full-stack blogging platform where people write, publish and discuss articles, with secure cookie-based login, a rich text editor, image uploads, likes, bookmarks and comments.
description: PublishPro is a complete blogging platform built on the MERN stack. Anyone can browse and search articles; signed-in users can write posts in a rich text editor, upload a cover image, pick one of 42 categories and add tags. Readers can like, save and share posts, leave comments, and open an author's page to see their bio, stats and everything they have published. Each writer gets a profile dashboard with total blogs, likes, views and saves, and can edit or delete their own posts.

Security was a main focus. Login uses a short-lived JWT access token and a 7-day refresh token, both stored in httpOnly cookies so JavaScript can never read them. Every refresh token is tied to a session record in MongoDB, so sessions can be revoked: logging out, 'log out of all devices' and changing a password all invalidate them, and expired sessions are removed automatically by a TTL index. On the client, an Axios interceptor quietly refreshes an expired token and replays any requests that failed in the meantime, so users are never logged out mid-task. Passwords are hashed with bcrypt, a forgot-password flow emails a 15-minute reset link, admin routes are protected by role, and all article HTML is sanitised with DOMPurify before it is shown.

The REST API is built with Express 5 and Mongoose. Likes, bookmarks and view counts use atomic MongoDB updates so two quick clicks can't corrupt a count, and logged-in readers are only counted once per post. Author statistics are calculated with an aggregation pipeline, so like and save lists never leave the database. Search matches titles, tags, categories and author names, with user input escaped before it reaches a regex. Images are streamed from memory to Cloudinary through Multer, with a 5 MB limit and an image-only filter.

Performance and mobile use were treated as features. The home feed is paginated on the server and returns only the fields a card needs, which cut that response from 36 KB to 1.3 KB. Pages are code-split so the editor only downloads when someone writes, responses are gzip-compressed, database indexes back the common queries, and Cloudinary serves resized WebP/AVIF thumbnails instead of full-size photos. The CSS is written mobile-first, with a collapsible navbar, a profile menu that folds away on phones and a phone-friendly editor toolbar, and was checked at phone, tablet and desktop widths.
highlights: Full CRUD for blogs with a TinyMCE rich text editor, cover images, categories and tags
JWT access + refresh tokens in httpOnly cookies with server-side sessions that can be revoked
Silent token refresh in an Axios interceptor that queues and replays failed requests

Search across titles, tags, categories and authors, with server-side pagination

Home feed response cut from 36 KB to 1.3 KB; main JS bundle cut by about 29%
Code splitting, gzip, database indexes and Cloudinary WebP/AVIF thumbnails
Mobile-first responsive design, deployed on Render

points: Built a full-stack MERN blogging platform with a REST API, rich text editing, Cloudinary image uploads, likes, bookmarks, comments, search and author dashboards.

Used atomic MongoDB updates and an aggregation pipeline for likes, views and author stats, sanitised user HTML with DOMPurify, and built a mobile-first UI that works across phones, tablets and desktops.

portfolio.shortDescription: A full-stack URL shortener where every user gets their own link space, with custom short codes, click tracking, secure cookie-based login and email verification.
description: URL Shortener turns long links into short ones that are easy to share. After signing up, users paste a URL, optionally pick a custom short code such as 'portfolio', and get a link like yoursite.com/vyom/portfolio. From a dashboard they can copy a link in one tap, share it through the phone's native share sheet, edit where it points, delete it and search their links. Every visit is counted, so each link shows its clicks and the profile page shows total clicks across all links.

Each user has their own namespace. Short links are built from a username plus a code, so two people can both own '/gh' and each one opens the right destination. Users can choose their own username from the profile page, with live validation and a warning that changing it breaks links already shared. Codes are unique per user through a compound MongoDB index, and the app moved the database from its old site-wide unique index to the per-user one automatically on startup, while links shared in the old format keep working.

Security was a main focus. Login uses a short-lived JWT access token and a 7-day refresh token, both in httpOnly cookies, and every refresh token is tied to a session record in MongoDB, so logging out really ends the session. Passwords are hashed with Argon2. New accounts verify their email with an 8-digit code or a link, and a forgot-password flow emails a single-use reset link that expires after 15 minutes. Reset tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes, and the reset page shows the same message whether or not an email exists, so it can't be used to find accounts. Every edit and delete checks that the link belongs to the signed-in user, only http and https URLs are accepted, and usernames and codes can't take over the app's own pages such as /login.

The server follows an MVC structure with separate routes, controllers, services, models and Zod validators, and is deployed on Vercel as a serverless Express app. The EJS views were built mobile-first, with a bottom tab bar on phones, large tap targets, 16px inputs so iPhones don't zoom, automatic dark mode, inline error and success messages, and forms that keep what the user typed after an error. Every page was checked at phone and desktop widths.
highlights: Create, edit, delete and search short links, with custom or random short codes
Per-user namespaces (/username/code), so two users can use the same code
Custom usernames with live preview, reserved-word checks and uniqueness validation
Click tracking per link and total clicks on the profile
One-tap copy with a fallback for plain http, plus the native Web Share API on phones
JWT access + refresh tokens in httpOnly cookies, backed by revocable MongoDB sessions
Argon2 password hashing, email verification and a forgot/reset password flow
Single-use reset links stored as SHA-256 hashes, with no way to test which emails have accounts
Ownership checks on every link action, and only http/https URLs allowed
Zod validation on every form, with friendly error messages
Responsive HTML emails built with MJML and sent through Resend
Mobile-first UI with a bottom tab bar, dark mode, custom 404 and error pages
MVC structure, deployed on Vercel as a serverless Express app

resume.heading: URL Shortener | Node.js, Express, MongoDB, EJS
points: Built a full-stack URL shortener with custom or random short codes, per-link click tracking, one-tap copy and share, and a searchable dashboard, using an MVC structure with Express 5 and Mongoose.

Designed per-user link namespaces (/username/code) backed by a compound unique MongoDB index, so users can share the same short code, and migrated the live database from a site-wide unique index without breaking existing links.

Protected user data with ownership checks on every link action, Zod validation on all forms and http/https-only URLs, and built a mobile-first EJS interface with dark mode, deployed on Vercel.

portfolio.shortDescription: A LaTeX-inspired résumé editor with a live preview, autosave and one-click PDF export.
description: Resume Builder turns writing a résumé into something closer to writing code. The left pane is styled like a LaTeX source file, with commands such as \name and \title and section comments, while the right pane shows the finished, print-ready résumé updating as you type. When it looks right, one click exports it as a clean PDF.

You can add as many experience, project, education and certification entries as you need, upload an optional profile photo, and list your skills as tags. Empty sections are hidden automatically, so the final document only shows what you've filled in. Everything is saved in the browser as you go, so closing the tab never loses your work.

Under the hood, each section is defined by a small schema, and one set of generic functions creates, reads and renders every section, so adding a new section means adding one schema entry. Entry cards are cloned from HTML templates, the preview is rebuilt by a debounced compile step, and all user input is HTML-escaped before it reaches the page. The whole app runs inside a strict-mode IIFE with no dependencies.
highlights: Live, debounced preview with a compile status indicator
Unlimited entries for experience, projects, education and certifications
One-click PDF export with print-specific CSS
Input escaping to prevent HTML injection

portfolio.shortDescription: A responsive React food ordering site with Firebase sign-in, a category-filtered menu, a live cart and a full checkout flow.
description: FoodZing is a food ordering website built with React. Visitors can browse 36 dishes across 8 categories, such as Salad, Rolls, Desserts and Pasta, and filter the menu with one tap on a category. Dishes are added to the cart straight from the menu card, with plus and minus controls that update the quantity and the running total instantly.

Users create an account or sign in through Firebase Authentication. After signing in, the navbar greets them by name. From the cart they see an itemised bill with subtotal, delivery fee and total, then fill in a validated delivery form to place the order. The site also includes About, Why FoodZing and Contact sections, and the contact form sends messages to a Firebase Realtime Database.

Under the hood, cart state lives in a React Context, so every component reads and updates it from one place. Auth state is tracked once at the app level and passed down. The site uses HashRouter so it runs on GitHub Pages without server rewrites, and a custom hook handles smooth scrolling to page sections from any route. The layout is fully responsive, from a hamburger menu and stacked hero on phones to a multi-column grid on desktops.
highlights: Category filter across 36 dishes in 8 categories
Add to cart with live quantity controls and running total
Sign up and login with Firebase Authentication
Personalised navbar greeting for signed-in users
Itemised cart and validated checkout form
Fully responsive layout with a mobile hamburger menu
Deployed on GitHub Pages using HashRouter

resume.heading: FoodZing | React, Firebase, CSS
points: Built a responsive food ordering web app in React with a category-filtered menu of 36 dishes, a live cart and a validated checkout flow.
Managed global cart state with the Context API and integrated Firebase Authentication for sign-up, login and personalised user sessions.
Deployed to GitHub Pages using HashRouter and a custom smooth-scroll hook, with a mobile-first layout that adapts from phones to desktops.

projects.title: The Maroons: A Rakhi Store
projects.subtitle: A WhatsApp Ordering Store for a Home Business

portfolio.shortDescription: A mobile-first online store for a real home business selling handmade rakhis, with custom name rakhis and one-tap ordering on WhatsApp.
description: The Maroons is a real online store for a small home business in Himatnagar that makes handmade Jeco Moti rakhis. Customers browse 69 designs in four types, add them to a cart, and send the whole order to the owner on WhatsApp in one tap. There is no server or online payment: the order arrives as a ready-written WhatsApp message, which is how the business already works.

Customers can also design a custom name rakhi. They add as many names as they need, see each name drawn letter by letter as beads on the maroon thread, and choose a Moti colour from close-up photos of the real beads, so there are no surprises about colour. Custom rakhis go into the same cart as ready-made ones and are sent in the same message, with every name spelled out letter by letter.

The site is built to protect the business as well as to sell. An Order Terms page covers making time, cancellations, pickup deadlines and spelling responsibility, and customers must agree to the terms before the order is sent. The agreement is written into the WhatsApp message itself. A 'How to Order' timeline with example chat bubbles explains the whole flow, from sending the order to the 'ready for pickup' message.

Under the hood, the cart and customer details are kept in React Context and saved to localStorage, and one function builds the WhatsApp order message so it can be unit tested. The site uses clean URLs on GitHub Pages through a 404 redirect, and the CSS is written mobile-first, with a slide-in menu, a sticky type slider and a sticky buy bar on phones. Product photos were auto-cropped around each rakhi and compressed from about 180 MB to about 2 MB.
highlights: One-tap ordering: the whole cart is sent as a ready-written WhatsApp message
Custom name rakhis with a live bead preview and real bead-colour photos
Ready-made and custom rakhis in one cart, saved in the browser
Order Terms page and required agreement, recorded in every order
English-only name check and a required spelling confirmation for custom orders
'How to Order' timeline with WhatsApp-style chat bubbles
Mobile-first design with a slide-in menu, sticky type slider and sticky buy bar
Same-type product recommendations, tap-to-zoom photos and price sorting
Images cut from about 180 MB to about 2 MB, and clean URLs on GitHub Pages
Unit tests for the cart, required terms and the WhatsApp order message

resume.heading: The Maroons Rakhi Store | React, React Router, Context API
points: Built and launched a mobile-first React store for a real home business, where customers send their whole cart as a pre-written WhatsApp order, with no server or payment gateway.
Developed a custom name rakhi builder with a live bead preview, real bead-colour photos and spelling checks, feeding into the same cart and order message as ready-made products.
Protected the business with an Order Terms page and a required agreement recorded in every order, and cut page weight by about 99% (180 MB to 2 MB) by auto-cropping and compressing 69 product photos.
